steps.text: Toss grated potatoes with flour in a large bowl. Stir in mashed potatoes until combined.
Whisk egg and milk together in a separate bowl; mix into the potatoes. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Drop in potato mixture, forming patties about 2 inches in diameter. Fry on both sides until golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Irish Boxty
raw_recipe.description: Boxty is a traditional Irish potato pancake made with grated and mashed potatoes; pan-fry until golden and crispy on the outside and fluffy inside.
raw_recipe.name: Irish Boxty

review.reviewBody: Crisp on the outside. Tender on the inside. MMMMM! To make these up faster for a brunch, I par-poiled the shredded potatoes for 3 minutes in a big pot of water, then drained well before mixing with the rest of the ingredients. This way, I could cook them for a shorter time at a higher temp, so they were even crispier. You have to dry this recipe for your next brunch!

I used a half of 3.2 oz Hungry Jack Hashbrown Potatoes instead of fresh potatoes. Added…1/2 c shred cheese, 2 strips cut up bacon. Fried in air fryer. Sprayed bottom of drawer & top of potatoes with olive oil. Cooked for 9 minutes @ 350 degrees. Full disclosure…. They were a little dry. I’d add a little more milk. Served with buttermilk dressing & sour cream.
As is, pretty good! The second time I made them I added some minced onion and garlic and about a cup of sharp cheddar and they were to die for!!! Thank you for sharing this recipe!!

Delicious Potato Cakes! Very easy to make, great for beginner cooks. Tip: portion them in the frying pan on the thinner side. A few of my Boxtys were too thick and not as crispy as the thinner ones. I used 2% milk vs skim milk and the only addition I made was to top with a sprinkling of chopped chives and a dollop of sour cream. My husband’s tip is to top with a little (or a lot) of maple syrup!!

I make this from leftover mashed potatoes. I add onion salt, pepper, flour and an egg. Mix all together and if it is too thick add a little half and half or milk. I spray my skillet with pam and drop by the spoon full and fry until golden brown. I serve it with butter and more salt and pepper if needed. My aunt made this for me when I was a small child and I have always loved them. I am now ready for my 50th wedding anniversary so I have been making them for a long while. They are really good and gives another way to have potatoes.

I have tried several of the potato pancake/latke recipes. This one is my favourite. It's a great mix of mashed and grated potato, and I think the ratio of each is just right. Quick to make, and adjustments can be made to suit your preferences, like adding spices/seasonings, or grated onion and minced garlic, which I have also done. My husband devours them-never any leftovers. Thanks Brooke!

OMG!!! This Irish-Canadian gal loves her boxty..this is amasing! I only used 2 tablespoons of oil and I made 12 mini-boxty and they all came out golden brown and soft. Also I used spelt flour, I'm allergic to wheat (came out grand). Fed them to my sister and she said they reminded her of Ireland. We ate them with ketchup, but will definately come up with something a little more creative next time. Thanks!

These were great! I used a small batch of instant mashed potatoes since I didn’t have any leftover mashies and frozen hashbrowns for the potatoes. Next time I might add some shredded cabbage and onion to make more of a “bubble and squeak” for added heft. I served them with Greek yogurt and green onions as a side dish the first night, then turned leftovers into dinner the next night by adding smoked salmon and a halved soft-boiled egg atop each. Yum!

A simple and delicious recipe! It tastes great plain, but when I added a bit of onions to the batter, that made it even better. I am sure it is possible to add a bunch of other ingredients to spice things up and make it more interesting. The only thing I noticed is that I had to add a LOT of salt and pepper to taste a difference.

We absolutely loved this recipe. The recipe has such a fantastic potato flavor. We put some green onion, jalapeño, and garlic into the recipe for a spicier flavor. We will be making this a regular at our home.
Added green onion, cracked pepper and cheese curd.
I had just enough leftover dry instant mashed; I grated about 6 or 7 mini gold poatoes & went by recipe. I'm of Irish descent & never heard of this--sure & they came out lovely!
Yummy 😋
Definitely missing the onion.
I love these and I have made them before! I prefer mine with some minced onion and a little garlic powder with the salt and pepper.
Needs more flavour bit plain
Oh dear. I followed another recipe that didn't look quite right, but followed it anyway. No eggs, two cups of flour. Next time, I'll try yours. I want the potatoes, not the flour.

We just threw out our old potato pancake recipe for this one! So delicious. Perfect texture. We used this in our Irish breakfast, and let's just say, we will not be waiting for St Patrick's Day to roll around to make this again. Any leftover mashed potatoes will become boxty. This boxty.
I added a bit of thyme to the mixture and a bit of butter at the end.
Good recipe, I add the EVO to the batter and "dry fry" the cakes on my griddle! Delish! Not as oily!
